proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal requests additional millage to permit the continued levy by the intermediate school district of the maximum mills for special education previously approved by the electors.
Shall the limitation on the annual property tax rate for the education of students with a disability in Allegan Area Educational Service Agency, Michigan, be increased by 0.1699 mill ($0.1699 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 8 years, 2027 to 2034, inclusive (this increase will allow the intermediate school district to levy the maximum rate of 3.05 mills previously approved by the electors that has been reduced as required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963); the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $13,703,962 from local property taxes authorized herein?
proposals.officialTitle: ALLEGAN AREA EDUCATIONAL SERVICE AGENCY SPECIAL EDUCATION MILLAGE PROPOSAL (RESTORATION OF MILLAGE REDUCTION)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 0.1699 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.name: Comstock Charter Township Proposal to Renew Law Enforcement Millage
proposals.description: Renews the expired law-enforcement millage at up to 0.9920 mill for 2026–2029 (~$814K first year).
proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the expired previously voted charter millage for the Charter Township of Comstock of 1.0 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 taxable value) for law enforcement services, as reduced to .9920 mill ($0.9920 per $1,000 taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at up to .9920 mill ($0.9920 per $1,000 taxable value) and levied for four years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, to provide funds to be allocated for law enforcement services, a portion of which may be disbursed to Kalamazoo County or such other or fewer local units of government as the Township Board determines appropriate, which levy will raise an estimated $813,904 in the first year?
proposals.officialTitle: Comstock Charter Township Proposal to Renew Law Enforcement Millage
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 1 mill for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.

proposals.name: Comstock Public Schools Bond Proposal
proposals.description:
Shall Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty-Three Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($23,700,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:
erecting, completing and remodeling school buildings, facilities and additions to school buildings and facilities, including school safety and security improvements; equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and refurnishing school buildings…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty-Three Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($23,700,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:
erecting, completing and remodeling school buildings, facilities and additions to school buildings and facilities, including school safety and security improvements; equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and refurnishing school buildings and facilities; purchasing school buses; acquiring, installing, equipping and re-equipping school buildings for instructional technology; and preparing, developing, improving and equipping athletic fields, play fields, playgrounds, structures, facilities and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 0.43 mill ($0.43 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a 0.00 mill net increase over the prior year’s levy. The maximum number of years the bonds of any series may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is thirty (30) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.23 mills ($1.23 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.officialTitle: Comstock Public Schools Bond Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $23.7 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.name: A Proposal to Amend the Kalamazoo City Charter to Establish a Citizens' Advisory Healthcare Action Committee and Require a Healthcare Action Plan
proposals.description: Petition-initiated charter amendment creating a citizen advisory board to draft a local Healthcare Action Plan and recommend ways to lower costs and improve access. The board is advisory only — the city has no authority to implement health policy. Parallel measures appear in Lansing, East Lansing, Kalamazoo and Portage.
proposals.ballotLanguage:
A proposal to amend the Kalamazoo City Charter to establish a Citizens’ Advisory Healthcare Action Committee appointed by the City Commission to address healthcare affordability and access. The Committee would gather public testimony from the community; analyze data; review how federal, state, and local policies have affected healthcare affordability and access; and produce a biennial Healthcare Action Plan. The Healthcare Action Plan must evaluate changes in health insurance and benefit coverage, track actions of federal and state officials, and recommend solutions. The City Commission must adopt and publish a Healthcare Action Plan.
Shall this proposal be adopted?
proposals.officialTitle: A Proposal to Amend the Kalamazoo City Charter to Establish a Citizens' Advisory Healthcare Action Committee and Require a Healthcare Action Plan
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote adopts the change described in the ballot language.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current rules in place.
proposals.conservativeView: Creates a permanent new government body for a subject cities have no power over; the "plan" cannot be implemented and risks becoming an advocacy vehicle for single-payer-style policy.
proposals.progressiveView: Supporters say it gives residents a formal voice on healthcare affordability and pressures state and federal officials to act.

proposals.description:

erecting, completing and remodeling school buildings, facilities and additions to school buildings and facilities, including school safety and security improvements; equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and refurnishing school buildings…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty-Three Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($23,700,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:
erecting, completing and remodeling school buildings, facilities and additions to school buildings and facilities, including school safety and security improvements; equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and refurnishing school buildings and facilities; purchasing school buses; acquiring, installing, equipping and re-equipping school buildings for instructional technology; and preparing, developing, improving and equipping athletic fields, play fields, playgrounds, structures, facilities and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 0.43 mill ($0.43 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a 0.00 mill net increase over the prior year’s levy. The maximum number of years the bonds of any series may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is thirty (30) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.23 mills ($1.23 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.officialTitle: Comstock Public Schools Bond Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $23.7 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

Shall the limitation on the annual property tax rate for the education of students with a disability in Allegan Area Educational Service Agency, Michigan, be increased by 0.1699 mill ($0.1699 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 8 years, 2027 to 2034, inclusive (this increase will allow the intermediate school district to levy the maximum rate of 3.05 mills previously approved by the electors that has been reduced as required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963); the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $13,703,962 from local property taxes authorized herein?
proposals.officialTitle: ALLEGAN AREA EDUCATIONAL SERVICE AGENCY SPECIAL EDUCATION MILLAGE PROPOSAL (RESTORATION OF MILLAGE REDUCTION)
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 0.1699 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

proposals.name: A Proposal to Amend the Portage City Charter to Establish a Citizens’ Advisory Healthcare Action Board and Require a Healthcare Action Plan
proposals.description: Petition-initiated charter amendment creating a citizen advisory board to draft a local Healthcare Action Plan and recommend ways to lower costs and improve access. The board is advisory only — the city has no authority to implement health policy. Parallel measures appear in Lansing, East Lansing, Kalamazoo and Portage.
proposals.ballotLanguage:
A proposal to amend the City of Portage Charter to establish a Citizens’ Advisory Healthcare Action Board appointed by the City Council to address healthcare affordability and access. The Board would gather public testimony from the community; analyze data; review how federal, state, and local policies have affected healthcare affordability and access; and produce a biennial Healthcare Action Plan. The Healthcare Action Plan must evaluate changes in health insurance and benefit coverage, track actions of federal and state officials, and recommend solutions. The City Council must adopt and publish a Healthcare Action Plan.
Shall the proposed be adopted?
proposals.officialTitle: A PROPOSAL TO AMEND THE PORTAGE CITY CHARTER TO ESTABLISH A CITIZENS’ ADVISORY HEALTHCARE ACTION BOARD AND REQUIRE A HEALTHCARE ACTION PLAN
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote adopts the change described in the ballot language.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current rules in place.
proposals.conservativeView: Creates a permanent new government body for a subject cities have no power over; the "plan" cannot be implemented and risks becoming an advocacy vehicle for single-payer-style policy.
proposals.progressiveView: Supporters say it gives residents a formal voice on healthcare affordability and pressures state and federal officials to act.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
Shall Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County, Michigan, borrow the sum of not to exceed Twenty-Three Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars ($23,700,000) and issue its general obligation unlimited tax bonds therefor, in one or more series, for the purpose of:
erecting, completing and remodeling school buildings, facilities and additions to school buildings and facilities, including school safety and security improvements; equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and refurnishing school buildings and facilities; purchasing school buses; acquiring, installing, equipping and re-equipping school buildings for instructional technology; and preparing, developing, improving and equipping athletic fields, play fields, playgrounds, structures, facilities and sites?
The following is for informational purposes only:
The estimated millage that will be levied for the proposed bonds in 2027 is 0.43 mill ($0.43 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a 0.00 mill net increase over the prior year’s levy. The maximum number of years the bonds of any series may be outstanding, exclusive of any refunding, is thirty (30) years. The estimated simple average annual millage anticipated to be required to retire this bond debt is 1.23 mills ($1.23 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation).
(Pursuant to State law, expenditure of bond proceeds must be audited and the proceeds cannot be used for repair or maintenance costs, teacher, administrator or employee salaries, or other operating expenses.)
proposals.officialTitle: Comstock Public Schools Bond Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote authorizes the sale of $23.7 million in bonds, repaid through a property tax levy over the life of the bonds.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote rejects the borrowing — no bonds are issued and no new debt levy is added.
proposals.conservativeView: Bonds commit taxpayers to decades of debt service. Ask whether the project list is needs or wants, whether the district has maintained what it already has, and what the total interest cost will be. "No tax rate increase" often means extending an existing levy for many more years rather than letting it expire.
proposals.progressiveView: Bonds let communities fund major facility needs — safety, infrastructure, aging buildings — spreading the cost over the years the improvements will be used.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance and renews millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 19.9780 mills ($19.9780 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Schoolcraft Community Schools, Kalamazoo County, Michigan, be renewed for a period of 10 years, 2027 to 2036, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 18 mills are levied in 2027 is approximately $1,275,000 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy)?
proposals.officialTitle: Schoolcraft Community Schools Operating Millage Renewal Proposal
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 18 mills for 10 years — generally no increase over what you pay now.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.
proposals.progressiveView: Keeps an existing, voter-approved service funded at the same rate with no new tax.
